channel.title: Newsnavigator (English)
channel.description: We deliver the news. What you make of it is up to you.

item.title: New bomb threats hit flights and broadcasters across Europe
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Several flights in Europe have been disrupted by bomb threats over the past week, according to several outlets. Broadcasters in several countries also received threats, and no bombs were found at the affected sites, SCMP reports. (Sources: CNBC, Dawn, Bangkok Post, Meduza, Sveriges Radio Ekot)

item.title: Democrats win big in US midterm elections
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Several sources report that Democrats won by a wide margin in the US midterm elections. Fox News reports that James Talarico beat Ken Paxton in Texas by more than twelve percentage points. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Politico, Fox News, Axios, The Washington Post)

item.title: Democrats win US midterm elections
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrats won the US midterm elections, according to CGTN and Le Monde. CGTN says public anger over living costs, immigration crackdowns and the Iran war contributed to the result, while Al Jazeera writes that the Iran war helped Democrats win. (Sources: Al Jazeera, Vox, Le Monde (English), CGTN)

item.title: Netflix announces Stranger Things prequel set in the 1950s
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Netflix has announced a Stranger Things prequel, according to El País. The series Other Worlds is set to premiere in 2028 and will take place in Nevada in the 1950s. (Sources: El País América, Expressen Nöje, Aftonbladet Nöjesbladet)

item.title: Tankers carrying Russian diesel to US change course
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to Deutsche Welle, tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US are changing course because sanctions reportedly block docking. Trump says he met Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and predicts a big agreement before talks in Abu Dhabi. (Sources: The Straits Times, The Japan Times, Sveriges Radio Ekot, The Hindu, RT)

item.title: Around 30 killed in attack on market in Taiz, Yemen
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Around 30 people were killed in an attack on a market in Taiz province, Yemen, according to several sources. The Houthis say Saudi aircraft carried out the strikes. Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthis blame each other for the attack. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Middle East Eye, France 24, Sveriges Radio Ekot, The Hindu)

item.title: Melania Trump meets Russian and Ukrainian representatives at White House on Oleshky
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to Meduza, Melania Trump met Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House and received Ukraine's Order of Princess Olha. According to the Washington Examiner, a short ceasefire in Oleshky allowed hundreds of civilians to be evacuated. (Sources: The Kyiv Independent, France 24, El Tiempo, Sveriges Radio Ekot, Hindustan Times)

item.title: Democrats win US midterm elections
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrats won the US midterm elections, according to several sources. Several outlets address what the result could mean for AI data centres, with BBC Verify examining whether voters were influenced and South China Morning Post reporting analysts' warnings of tighter regulation. (Sources: Sveriges Radio Ekot, Hindustan Times, Al Jazeera, The Kyiv Independent, The Hindu)

item.title: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch in Washington for 14 days
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. A federal judge has ordered a 14-day pause on construction of Trump's triumphal arch in Washington. Several sources report that a federal planning commission had approved the project hours earlier, with an 8-4 vote according to Deutsche Welle. (Sources: El País América, BBC World, The Guardian, NPR, Hindustan Times)

item.title: Tech stocks fall on fears of AI rules after US midterms
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Tech stocks fell on Thursday after US midterm results sparked fears of tighter AI rules. Daily Maverick, citing Reuters, says the drop is the biggest since last year's sell-off. (Sources: Dawn, The Guardian, Al Jazeera, Yonhap, Nikkei Asia)

item.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has resigned after the collapse of Ueno Bank, according to several sources, which report that millions of customer accounts have been frozen. According to NPR and the BBC, lawmakers have voted to pursue impeachment proceedings against him. (Sources: Deutsche Welle, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, Hindustan Times, The Hindu)

item.title: Republicans look for those to blame after midterm defeat
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Republicans have lost the midterm elections, and according to El País they are looking for culprits without directly naming Trump. The president, according to the paper, blames the Iran war for the defeat while touting progress on the construction of a White House ballroom. (Sources: El País (English), El País América, MercoPress)

item.title: Nasdaq falls sharply after US midterms on AI concerns
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. The Nasdaq fell sharply after the US midterm elections, by 5.5 percent according to SCMP and Nikkei Asia. According to BBC, the concern is possible tougher scrutiny of data centres and the AI industry. (Sources: BBC World, Yonhap, South China Morning Post, Nikkei Asia, The National)

item.title: Vance says Iran war was reason Republicans lost midterms
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. US Vice President JD Vance says the Iran war was the real reason Republicans lost the midterm elections, according to several outlets. According to Middle East Eye, Israel's UN ambassador rejects his analysis. (Sources: El País América, Middle East Eye, Deutsche Welle, Al Jazeera, Hindustan Times)

item.title: Protests across France during nationwide strike over cost of living
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to the French interior ministry, about 600,000 people joined protests across France on 5 November, while unions say the figure was far higher. The protests focused on cost of living and public services, and Dawn reports clashes with police in Paris and Lyon. (Sources: El Tiempo, BBC World, Deutsche Welle, The Guardian, Dawn)

item.title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%, first increase in over three years
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. The Bank of England raised its benchmark rate to 4%, according to The Guardian. Dawn reports the move was a quarter-point rise, the first since 2023, aimed at fighting inflation driven up by soaring energy costs. (Sources: The Guardian, Dawn, The Wall Street Journal)

item.title: Republicans lose control of Congress in US midterms
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to several outlets, Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterms, and Trump enters his last two years as a lame duck. The Straits Times reports that Trump said he would work with Democrats while keeping his veto powers. (Sources: France 24, South China Morning Post, Deutsche Welle, The Straits Times, Buenos Aires Times)

item.title: Vance says Iran war was behind Republican midterm losses
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Vice President JD Vance says the war against Iran was the reason Republicans lost the midterm elections, according to several sources. Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon rejects the claim, while Trump, according to SVT, says the war was worth it. (Sources: Washington Examiner, Middle East Eye, Hindustan Times, BBC World, The Hindu)

item.title: Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Democrats have won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the 2026 midterm elections, according to several outlets. Fox News reports Democrats gained seven Senate seats and 27 House seats, while Buenos Aires Times reports at least seven Senate seats. (Sources: CNBC, Washington Examiner, Al Jazeera, NPR, Fox News)

item.title: Republicans lose midterm elections: Trump reacts to the results
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to Axios, Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections. Hindustan Times reports that Trump did not join aides when the results came in, and Axios writes that he returned to Washington construction projects. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Axios, Africanews, The New York Times, Tehran Times)

item.title: Democrats win control of US Congress in midterm elections
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Democrats took control of both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections, according to several sources including the Buenos Aires Times and South China Morning Post. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell after the vote, Hindustan Times reports. (Sources: The Guardian, CNBC, The Daily Caller, NPR, The Wall Street Journal)

item.title: Netanyahu alleges foreign interference in Israel election
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Netanyahu raises concerns about foreign interference and calls for an investigation, according to Hindustan Times and France 24. Israel's election commission rejects his fraud claims, according to The Hindu and The Guardian. (Sources: Hindustan Times, France 24, The Hindu, The Guardian, Fox News)

item.title: Ibero-American foreign ministers back Argentina's Falklands claim at Madrid summit
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously approved a communiqué backing Argentina's sovereignty claim over the Falklands and calling for resumed negotiations, according to MercoPress. Zelenskyy, according to his own Telegram post, has arrived in Spain for talks on air defence and meetings during the summit. (Sources: MercoPress, El País América, Mexico News Daily, Africanews, Al-Monitor)

item.title: Democrats take control of both Senate and House in US midterms
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to Middle East Eye, the Democrats have taken control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the US midterm elections, by wide margins. Hindustan Times writes that the Iran war, gas prices and Trump's miscalculations led to the result. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Middle East Eye, The Straits Times, France 24, Le Monde (English))

item.title: ANC leads early results in South Africa's local elections
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Voting in South Africa's local elections took place on November 4 and counting has begun. According to The Straits Times, the ANC leads early, preliminary results with a sharply reduced share of the vote, and the election authority expects final results by Sunday. (Sources: The East African, Africanews, The Guardian, Dagens Nyheter, CGTN)

item.title: Democrats reportedly take US Senate majority as Mississippi and Alaska races remain undecided
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to Hindustan Times, CGTN and Axios, Democrats have won a majority in the US Senate in the midterm elections. Al Jazeera reports that results in Mississippi and Alaska were delayed. (Sources: The Guardian, Middle East Eye, The Hindu, CNA, Hindustan Times)

item.title: Democrats take control of US Congress in midterm elections
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Democrats took control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the US midterm elections, according to several sources. The Wall Street Journal reports that the party also won a majority of governorships. (Sources: Hindustan Times, The Straits Times, Buenos Aires Times, Al Jazeera, The Hill)

item.title: Democrats take control of US Congress in midterm elections
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Several sources report that Democrats have taken control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the US midterm elections. The sources link the result to Trump's policies, including the war in Iran and economic issues such as fuel prices. (Sources: Vox, Hindustan Times, Le Monde (English), Tehran Times)

item.title: Democrats win both the Senate and the House in US midterm elections
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House in the US midterm elections, according to several sources. Outlets report on reactions on social media, on Wall Street and abroad, and on renewed scrutiny of President Trump's tariffs and healthcare cuts. (Sources: The Hindu, CNBC, Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal)

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race over Republican Mike Rogers, according to AP and US networks, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. According to Reuters, the US president repeatedly called him a jihadist during the campaign. (Sources: Hindustan Times, The Hindu, Daily Maverick, Axios, Tehran Times)

item.title: Israel's president begins talks with party leaders on forming a government
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Israeli President Isaac Herzog has started talks with party leaders about who will be given the mandate to form a government, according to DR. The New York Times reports the question is whether Netanyahu or Eisenkot can form the government. (Sources: DR Nyheder, Fox News, The New York Times, The National)

item.title: Democrats win control of US Congress in midterm elections
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to NPR, Democrats have won both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections. The Wall Street Journal reports that the party also won a majority of governorships. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Politico, Fox News, Axios, The Washington Post)

item.title: Talarico projected to win Texas Senate seat in midterms
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrat James Talarico is projected to win a US Senate seat in Texas in the midterm elections, according to Africanews. Hindustan Times reports that Talarico and Gina Hinojosa won their respective races and celebrated at a Whataburger. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Africanews, Mexico News Daily, The Hindu, Axios)

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, becoming first Muslim elected to US Senate
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race over Republican Mike Rogers, according to media projections cited by several outlets, and becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. A Reuters report describes attacks during the campaign, including from President Trump. (Sources: Al-Monitor, The Straits Times, Hindustan Times, Axios)

item.title: Republicans lose control of US Congress in election
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to The Wall Street Journal, Republicans lost control of Congress in Tuesday's election amid widespread frustration over the economy. The New York Times reports on Americans explaining why they rejected Trump's Republican Party. (Sources: The Hindu, Daily Maverick, Fox News, Hindustan Times, The New York Times)

item.title: Trump-backed Senate candidates lose key races
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Trump-backed Republican candidates lost key Senate races in South Carolina, North Carolina, Texas and Michigan, according to Dawn and Daily Maverick. Daily Maverick reports that the results give Democrats control of the Senate. (Sources: Dawn, Daily Maverick, Hindustan Times, The Japan Times)

item.title: Democrats win House and Senate in US midterms
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to DW, Democrats win control of the House and Senate in the US midterm elections. Axios and the Financial Times report internal conflict among Republicans, and Axios says members are questioning whether Speaker Mike Johnson can survive upcoming leadership elections. (Sources: Premium Times, The Hindu, Hindustan Times)

item.title: After US midterms, several voices expect no quick change in US policy
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. According to The Straits Times, a senior Canadian minister says the US midterms will not change Ottawa's stance on trade talks. Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, says, according to Dawn, that those expecting a shift in US policy are mistaken. (Sources: The Straits Times, South China Morning Post, Dawn, France 24, The National)

item.title: South Africa votes in local elections
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Local elections are under way in South Africa on Wednesday, according to several outlets. Voters in Johannesburg raise water, electricity and service concerns, and the BBC reports residents are tired of poor service quality. (Sources: AllAfrica, The Rio Times, Daily Maverick)

item.title: Russia bombards Ukraine's power grid ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Russia struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure with missiles and drones, according to Reuters, a week before US-brokered talks. Witkoff says the US, Russia and Ukraine will hold talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. (Sources: Al-Monitor, Euractiv, The Hindu, CGTN)

item.title: All 69 victims of Spanish train crash identified
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Spanish authorities have identified all 69 people killed in a high-speed train collision in Urda, central Spain, on 28 October, according to several outlets. Two Japanese nationals are among the dead, according to The Straits Times and The Japan Times. (Sources: El Tiempo, Politico Europe, El País (English), The New York Times)

item.title: 69 dead in Spanish train crash, twelve of them foreign nationals
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. According to Spanish authorities, as reported by The Guardian, 69 people died in the train crash on 28 October, 54 of them Spanish. Twelve foreign nationals are among the dead, four of them from the United States, according to several outlets. (Sources: El País América, BBC World, El Tiempo, Deutsche Welle, The Guardian)

item.title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts down
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. The independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta is closing, its editors say. The Straits Times and The Hindu attribute the closure to state and Kremlin pressure, and Meduza reports that journalists said the paper was to be evicted from its Moscow office the day before. (Sources: The Hindu, Hindustan Times, Meduza, The Straits Times, The Kyiv Independent)

item.title: One dead and six injured in shooting at Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Police said one person was killed and six injured when a gunman opened fire at a Spirit Halloween store in a mall in Fairfield, California, on Friday evening. According to Dawn, investigators had not yet identified the person responsible. (Sources: ABC News (Australien), El País América, NPR, The Rio Times, El Tiempo)

item.title: Polish president calls crisis meeting after clash at court
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. Polish President Karol Nawrocki calls a crisis meeting after unrest at the constitutional court, according to Swedish Radio's Ekot. According to Ekot, the government tried on Friday to remove the court's head, and thousands of demonstrators gathered outside the building. (Sources: Hindustan Times, The Hindu, The Straits Times, Politico Europe, Euractiv)

item.title: Actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Actor Patrick Stewart has died aged 86, according to several outlets, including Reuters and Deutsche Welle. He was known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. (Sources: Ars Technica, The Hindu, El País América, Aftonbladet Nöjesbladet, Daily Maverick)

item.title: Scottish police investigate Andrew and Epstein's time at Balmoral
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. Scottish police are investigating Andrew and Epstein's time at Balmoral. Media reports say the inquiries relate to claims that women were trafficked to the estate. (Sources: The Hindu, NRK, The New York Times)

item.title: Spain train crash leaves at least 69 dead near Toledo
item.description: AI, reviewed in Swedish by the editors. At least 69 people have died after a high-speed train hit the back of a stationary train near Toledo, Spain, on Wednesday, according to several outlets. Spain has begun three days of mourning, and search and rescue work in the wreckage continues. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Sveriges Radio Ekot, The Straits Times)

item.title: Christine Lagarde to step down as ECB president early, effective 7 February 2027
item.description: AI, not manually reviewed. The European Central Bank (ECB) announced on Thursday that Christine Lagarde will leave her post as president on 7 February 2027, almost nine months before her term ends in October. According to European Council President Antonio Costa, the successor search has begun. (Sources: El País América, MercoPress, The Wall Street Journal)
